Definition: from G69; sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake:--watch.
BiblicalUsage: Agrypnia is sleeplessness — watchings — and it appears twice, both in Paul's list of his sufferings as a minister of God: 'in watchings, in fastings,' and again, 'in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.' The word is not about insomnia but about nights spent awake for the gospel — travelling, praying, working, and watching over the churches.
TheologicalSignificance: Paul lists his watchings among his sufferings, and this word only names the sleepless nights — the apostle's endurance is the sermon.
